Therefore, a writer should never say they are solely a poet, a novelist, essayist, memoir writer, or playwright.

This course will provide opportunities for students to connect, create, and understand how diverse perspectives enrich the creative process. No pre-requisite required. This course provides 0.5 elective credit, not fine arts credit.

They will implement simple algorithms, store data in variables and arrays, and control program flow using conditional and iterative control structures. They will design software solutions to solve problems from various application areas.

This course is recommended for students who received a composite score of 2.0 (C) in Computer Programming 1, Computer Science Principles 1, or Robotics.

We will focus on comparative anatomy and adaptations to explore animals from the most simple to the most complex. This class will build on skills and content from Integrated Biology.

The emphasis of the class will be on strategy, technology, motivation, and impact of the U.S. military abroad and at home. Students read, research, analyze, discuss, write, and present their views based on facts, principles, and beliefs.

Students will research, determine reliability, identify bias, and describe evidence supporting varied perspectives on issues. Students will be expected to articulate opinions and support perspectives with meaningful and trustworthy evidence. This course includes an in-depth unit of global climate patterns and changes as well as field trips and guest speakers. Upperclassmen may earn 4 college credits through Northern Vermont University for successful completion of this course.

In the fall, students will analyze key historical and contemporary movements, with special attention to U.S. organizing in the 1960s and 70s. In the spring, the students will identify a current policy issue at the district, city, or state level and work together on a class-led campaign. description: This course is set up to expose students to basic Engineering concepts, Computer Aided Drafting (CAD) and Woodworking principles. The ﬁrst 6 weeks of the course are spent introducing students to basic engineering and design principles and an introduction to our 3D CAD program, ONShape. After gaining some basic skills in CAD, students will design and print a 3D object on our 3D printer. After acquiring basic knowledge and skills students will then design a woodworking project of their choice. During that time they will also learn the use and safety associated with all the woodworking machines a

rationale: Woodworking II: extension with CAD and design
description: This course is an extension of the Woodworking & Design I course. Students will come into this class with a certain set of skills and prior knowledge they acquired in the previous course. All students will start by doing an introductory unit in Architectural design using an application called Envisioneer. After that, students will continue with more advanced woodworking, and also be introduced to turning with the lathe, welding, creating more advanced 3D parts using OnShape. rationale: Flexible pathway: earn PE credit through self-directed activities
description: As part of the Flexible Pathway Program here at MHS students are provided the opportunity to earn physical education credit through activities they are passionate about. In a nutshell, students must complete 4 hours per week of said activity and identify a skill from that activity to master over the 18 week semester. Additionally students will write reﬂections, log hours and participate in a local community event centered around physical activity. description: In this semester-long course, students will explore the products and practices of different regions of the Spanish-speaking world through the lens of food. Through this exploration they will come to better understand the relationship between food and cooking in the Spanish-speaking world and the perspectives of various Spanish-speaking cultures. Semester 1 regions include: Spain, the Caribbean, and the Southern Cone. Semester 2 regions include: Mexico and the Andes. description: This semester-long course will be a hands-on project with a three-fold mission: 1. Learn a variety of job skills, and build ownership: Running a food cart business includes managing a budget, marketing, developing menus, purchasing, safe food handling, food prepping and cooking, scheduling and stafﬁng. Students will demonstrate their proﬁciency in several of these skills. 2. description: This course is to be taken along with Algebra I and it offers support, resources and extra time for students to complete work from the core class. Students will receive extra exposure to all the same math concepts taught in class in order to strengthen their understanding of the material. This course is a year long but students may be able to enter or exit at the semester mark.

rationale: Creative writing workshop offered grades 9-12; possible mastery English.
description: Creative Writing is a one-semester workshop designed to develop the expressive writing abilities of students. The course exposes students to many forms of excellent literature, both contemporary and classic, from many cultural traditions, as models for their own work. The focus is on poetry and short fiction. All genres will be read during the entire semester, apropos to any theme under discussion. The writing process, emphasized by means of the writing workshop, defines the way the course runs.

The course is founded on the idea that an enjoyment for reading comes from choice, so students will self-select their independent reading books. Class time will be used to read independently, discuss readings, learn and practice reading strategies, and talk about the reading process. Students will be expected to read each night for homework.

description: This course introduces philosophy through reading and discussing various philosophical understandings about the nature of the world and the people who inhabit it. The course emphasizes using philosophy as a tool to interpret the self, problems, and literature.

rationale: Seminar on modern global and American social history; partial world history.
description: This seminar style course asks students to grapple aloud with the leading aspects of modern Global and American social history from the early 1990s to the present. Attention is given to social, cultural and intellectual trends as well as political and economic issues, leadership, and ethical questions. This course also focuses on what is unique in the modern American experience and relates modern American experience to the broader global context. rationale: State history course; partial US history content.
description: Vermont History is a semester-long course that explores selected topics in the history of our home state from its first settlement by Native Americans, to the present day. While the course will follow a general chronological framework, treating each major historical period in turn, students will be encouraged to explore topics of personal interest to them in any historical period, or across several periods.

rationale: Integrated Math 1 core course; algebra content, possible Algebra I.
description: Integrated Math 1 is a first level course in a core curriculum of high school mathematics. Students will explore topics in number and quantity, algebra and statistics. Topics of study in this course include: exploring and communicating mathematics; simplifying expressions, solving equations and systems of equations; problem solving; coordinates and functions; proportional thinking; properties of linear functions; and two and three dimensional geometry.

rationale: Integrated Math 2 core course; geometry content, possible.
description: Integrated Math 2 is a second level course in a core curriculum of high school mathematics. Students will explore additional topics in algebra, geometry, and mathematical computation. Topics of study in this course include: quadratic and exponential functions and graphs; special triangle relationships including introduction to trigonometry.

rationale: Grade 9 integrated physical science with hands-on labs; Earth systems content.
description: In this course, you will explore how scientists investigate the natural world to explain the physics and chemistry of Earth. You will study the properties of matter and chemical reactions, explore forces and energy in motion, and deepen your understanding of Earth systems and resource management. Through hands-on labs and inquiry-based projects, you will build skills in modeling, data analysis, and problem-solving to explain and apply scientific ideas.

rationale: Forensic lab exercises in evidence analysis; physical/chemical content implied.
description: Students will learn selected techniques used in forensic investigations. They will apply those techniques to crime scenes and evidence analysis. The course will include laboratory exercises in evidence collection, analysis, and the application of forensic techniques in fiction.

rationale: Vermont ecosystems with hands-on environmental monitoring; ecology possible.
description: In Vermont Ecology, explore and learn about the Vermont ecosystem and the current environmental issues in the state. This course will focus on both freshwater aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Students will learn about the history of the Vermont ecosystem and explore the current state of Lake Champlain and feeding watersheds and the Vermont forest through hands-on environmental monitoring methods. After becoming more informed, get ready to discuss the future of Vermont and form opinions about current management and issues. Develop a plan to move our state forward.

Students will work through various programming projects using these devices, and may have the opportunity to develop their own products and program them to complete a task.

rationale: Yearbook production with writing and layout; possible English credit.
description: This class will produce the Mt. Abraham school yearbook, Aerie, using Josten’s Yearbook Avenue. Students will learn basic techniques for journalism, photography, advertising, marketing, and layout. Students will learn essential communication and collaboration skills, while working closely with their classmates to produce the yearbook. Students electing this course are expected to spend time after school, weekends, and during vacations in order to meet deadlines for publication.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School

description: Students will learn professional quality software used to retouch photos, color and manipulate images. Students begin with a tutorial to learn the software tools and then apply these skills to solve visual design problems. This course can be used to complete an Art or Tech credit.

rationale: Quilting and sewing craft; fine-arts claim keeps ARTS possible.
description: This course offers students the chance to be creative in the historical art forms of quilting, and sewing. Hand Sewing and machine sewing will be explored through various projects. Other crafts including knitting, crocheting, needlepoint, stenciling, stamping, etc. will be introduced. Students who have not taken the course in the past will have priority for admission. If space is available a student may, with teacher permission, take the course a second time.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Contemporary issues including federal budget and policy; partial civics.
description: This course provides a thematic study of current issues in the United States and worldwide. Issues will include the federal budget, crime and security, education, health care, immigration, poverty, terrorism, the global environment, international trade, weapons proliferation and defense. Students will experience a variety of learning activities including debates, simulations, mapping, research assignments, guest speakers and field trips. Prerequisites: SS1 and SS2.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Basic arithmetic review; below high-school math, possible elective.
description: This course develops and strengthens student understanding of operations of whole numbers, decimal numbers, fractions and integers. Other topics include percents, perimeter and volume, and some basic Geometry concepts. Students will solidify their understanding of basic mathematics so that they can move forward into Foundations of Algebra. Prerequisite: Teacher recommendation; MAP scores below 210.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Algebra/geometry foundation connections; applied consumer-level math.
description: The goal of this course is to connect the information provided in the two previous foundation level courses and to apply it to uses outside the classroom. Topics covered are triangular ratios, geometric proportions, the simplification of roots, algebraic computation of functions, and the connection of variables to more geometric problems. Prerequisite: Map scores between 220-230.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School

description: AP Environmental Science is a hybrid course including hard science and methods in chemistry, biology, ecology, and earth systems; ethics and decision making; and law. Integrating information, writing scientifically, collaboration, and problem solving are stressed. Prerequisite: Algebra I, Biology or Teacher Recommendation.

Recommendation will be based on grades, attendance, math and writing skills and general enthusiasm. Earth science, physical science, physical science general, or a course acceptable to the administration/science department may be accepted in place of Unified Science for transfer students. Prerequisite: A grade of 85 in A-level English, enro

There is a special emphasis on problem solving, scientific method, mathematics and inquiry. Earth science, physical science, physical science general, or a course acceptable to the administration/science department may be accepted in place of Unified Science for transfer students. Prerequisite: Teacher recommendation.

rationale: Animal biology, genetics and nutrition; zoology-type content, possible.
description: This course focuses the students’ studies on the behavior, biology, nutrition, genetics, health, breeding and management of animals. Some main focuses of the course are animal anatomy, physiology, ecology, animal health, invasive species, animal behavior, zoonotic diseases, animal husbandry, animal nutrition, conservation, etc. This course will equip students with knowledge to pursue a variety of animal-centered professions or continue their education in fields such as veterinary medicine, animal husbandry, conservation management, and more. Prerequisite: Biology, Unified Science is recommende

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Environmental science; ecosystems and environmental issues.
description: This Rigorous course is intended to reach students, with an in-depth approach to the importance of environmental issues that face us today. Students will become aware of what these problems are, the causes and the total ramifications in solving them. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Chemistry with a minimum grade of 75.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: General unified science; earth, physical science and inquiry.
description: This course is a general survey of earth and space sciences, physical science, and science inquiry. There is a special emphasis on problem solving and scientific method, with some mathematics and writing. This course will cover the material in a less-detailed manner than Unified Science with the focus on practical application of science concepts. Prerequisite: Teacher recommendation.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Astronomy elective with labs and hands-on exercises; narrow Earth/space elective.
description: This course will cover everything from finding constellations and planets in the sky to exploring quasars and black holes. The universe is a big place, so fun and interesting topics will not be in short supply. This course will include some demonstrations, labs and hands-on exercises.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Book club reading biography, classic novel and choice book; grades 9-12.
description: During this course students read one biography or autobiography, one book that is considered a classic novel, and one book of the student’s choice-for example, fantasy, romance, sports, or science fiction.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Current events reflecting global change; possible world history.
description: This course gives opportunity to reflect on the changes the world has undergone over the past several decades. This course allows students to examine the important political, social, and cultural trends of this era in history.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Stress management and wellness; health content, possible.
description: Handling stress can make life feel better, not just during school but after graduation as well. In this course, we use resources that are easily available, such as yoga, breathing, peer listening, and art projects to find greater ease of mind and body. We learn how to relax, manage our time, and negotiate to get what we need. This course is designed to help each person build habits for dealing with stressful situations.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
course_name: SB Harry Potter: Literary and Mythological Origins
rationale: Literary origins of Harry Potter; grades 9-12 literature elective.
description: This course will explore the archetypal texts, as well as the multi-media phenomenon. Drawing from sources such as Jane Austen, J.R. Tolkien, C.S. Lewis, Dorothy Sayers and many other notable authors, students will learn how their knowledge of various texts enhances their understanding. Through reading, writing, speaking, and listening, students will learn the significance of methodology. The course will offer literature-based instruction and provide students with an opportunity to explore fiction they enjoy. Excerpts of films will also be used to provide visual support.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Public speaking course; possible English credit.
description: The need to speak publicly presents itself in many areas such as job/college interviews, social events & school presentations. A goal of the 21st century learning expectations is: students “speak with clarity & effectiveness”, therefore this course will provide a challenging, diverse & relevant opportunity for all students. Individual speeches should interest the student, as well as, bring new awareness to the class as a whole.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Japanese culture course; culture-only content, possible.
description: This course reviews factors that make Japan a great power with world impact. Students study aspects of Japan’s culture today and in the past. These include, food, history, religion, value systems and the arts. Some language elements are included in the course. Students develop a personal interest through in-depth projects.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Print and broadcast journalism course; possible English credit.
description: This course is designed to help students gain knowledge of print and broadcast journalism and to apply journalistic style and integrity to their own stories. Students will analyze various newspapers as well as a class text. Interviewing skills will be developed. Students will write stories dealing with school and off-campus issues. Students will assess stories from their peers to develop editing skills. Legal and ethical boundaries will be explored.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Student rights and responsibilities, mock trials; civics content, possible.
description: This course is about student rights and responsibilities in the home, school and community. There will be videos, speakers, mock trials and selected readings.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Individualized math skills practice; essentials math, possible elective.
description: These courses address the individual math needs of students. IXL will be used to customize practice materials suited for immediate feedback on progress. Students MUST be recommended in order to enroll.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: Media analysis and reporting; grades 9-12, possible English credit.
description: Students will explore and evaluate the ways in which news is reported and portrayed across various media in the 21st century. Students will also learn how to report the news themselves across these forms of media, which may include: Newspaper, radio, television, social media, podcasts, and blogs.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
rationale: River watch and watershed study with lab; ecology and water quality, possible.
description: Water study includes a River Watch study, including information on the Hudson River watershed, macro and some micro organisms, water quality, geology and Roaring Branch as a laboratory. Prerequisite: Unified Science.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School

description: Water study includes a River Watch study, including information on the Hudson River watershed, macro and some micro organisms, water quality, geology and Roaring Branch as a laboratory. Prerequisite: Unified Science.

description: This course is available to those students who wish to write and share their poetry. Skills include the ability to listen well, read dramatically and interpret classical as well as contemporary poetry and its cultural function. Publication is a goal.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School

Students will practice showing respect while giving feedback to help their peers in the writing and editing process.

In the media literacy segment of the course, students will examine, speak about, and write about assessing credible news sources and identifying bias.

We will attempt to have live audiences for as many performances as possible.

This course incorporates primary sources, interactive activities, medieval art, and writing projects as part of the exploration and study.

rationale: American Civil War: war years 1861-1865; narrow US history elective.

This course is offered on alternate years, next offered in 26-27 SY.
